issues.title: A mammoth tour of Go's tooling for 2026
issues.html:
#​626 — November 27, 2026


Read the Web Version



Go Weekly





An Overview of Go's Tooling, Updated for 2026 — Alex's 2019 tour of Go tooling was one of our most popular links ever, but now he's back with an all-new 2026 edition. He covers numerous areas in detail from testing and code quality to benchmarking, refactoring, integrating with AI coding assistants, and more. An epic post!

Alex Edwards



Design Backend Systems That Scale — Every architecture decision is a tradeoff. Jem Young (Netflix) gives you a repeatable framework for scoping requirements, scaling data, and diagramming distributed systems, whether you’re on the job or in a system design interview.

master.dev sponsor



Yaegi v2: 'The Most Complete Go Interpreter' — Traefik's embeddable Go interpreter has been rewritten from scratch and in a simpler, more logical way with go/types and Go's SSA package doing the heavy lifting. It also passes 1044 of 1066 programs in Go's test suite (up from 641 previously).

Salleyron and Vauge (Traefik Labs)



IN BRIEF:

  • Go 1.28's scheduled development freeze has begun, with RC1 'tentatively scheduled' for the week of December 10.

  • Following last week's 'likely accept', the stable SIMD API is now enabled by default for Go 1.28, with GOEXPERIMENT=nosimdstable for turning it off.

  • Fixing a seven year old complaint, Go 1.28's GOCACHE build cache will trim itself as it grows to help keep the size in check.

  • JetBrains has opened up GoLand's code intelligence to VS Code and Cursor users in a free public beta preview.



How encoding/json/v2 Works Internally — The Go team's explained how the new JSON API works, but Jesús goes a bit deeper and follows a JSON document through the new stack, pointing out what's going on along the way.

Jesús Espino



Why Every Frontier Lab Uses Our Webhook Standard — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and xAI all sign webhooks the same way. See what each ships and why none rolled their own.

Svix sponsor



📄 Probabilistic Data Structures in Go – Part 2 – A follow-up to our featured item last week that moves on to binary fuse filters, UltraLogLog, MinHash and more. Anton Zhiyanov

📄 The Performance Penalty in Go's Default HTTP Client – Why two idle connections per host can have the kernel looking for free ports. Mansoor

📄 HTTP/3 From Scratch, Part 2 – Getting a browser to actually use HTTP/3, then building a full server and client in Go. Kevin McDonald

📄 Letting Packagers Override Your Go Program's Version Jamie Tanna



🛠 Code & Tools





gopgext: Write Postgres Extensions in Go — It's amazing what you can do with TinyGo and Jesús Espino has been experimenting a lot recently! gopgext uses a custom TinyGo target to turn plain Go (with marked functions becoming SQL functions) into Postgres extensions.

Jesús Espino



💡 And a way to write Linux kernel modules in Go too. Jesús's other experiment, gokm, takes a similar approach for building Linux kernel modules as a way to create devices, filesystems, network interfaces and more.



Ekuma: A Pure Go JavaScript Engine — From Ebitengine's creator comes a new, cgo-free JavaScript engine covering nearly all of ES2026 (the latest JavaScript language standard). It passes 99.99% of the test262 suite, and benchmarks ~8x faster than the more established goja.

Hajime Hoshi



errortype: Find Inconsistent Uses of Error Types — A linter that checks error types are used consistently as either a value or a pointer, as a mismatch can trip up errors.As. v0.0.12 can rename errors to Go's ErrX/XError conventions, and flags code that go vet will report if your go.mod uses 1.27+.

Fillmore Labs



tabc: Running Containers in Browser Tabs — A Go-built OCI runtime that runs containers on a WASM-compiled Linux kernel inside a headless Chromium instance making it possible to run images on a Mac, say, without needing a typical Linux VM. GitHub repo.

Farid Zakaria



  • Bubble Tea 2.2 – The popular TUI framework can now tell the terminal how to resume your program after a restart (via the OSC 7577 standard, which Rex and Herdr support).

  • go-redis 9.24 – The official Redis client library gains Redis 8.12 commands and an experimental Active-Active failover client.

  • gotreesitter 0.58 – Pure Go tree-sitter runtime whose output now matches C tree-sitter's for 34 grammars.

  • quic-go 0.66 – The pure Go QUIC and HTTP/3 implementation lands a large batch of RFC compliance fixes.

  • oapi-codegen 2.9 – Tool to generate Go clients/servers from OpenAPI specs.

  • Expr 1.18 – Expression language and evaluation engine for Go.



📰 Classifieds



CodeAF is one native Go binary that runs every coding task in its own isolated copy of the repo. #1 of ten on DeepSWE, lowest cost per fix.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • The Next.js team has merged an experimental Go-powered server, now called Switchyard, that sits in front of next start. It only proxies back to Node.js for now, but the plan is to move routing into Go.

  • minipg offers an interesting approach to using Postgres as a single executable, with a .pgdb directory holding the database. Could be a handy way to spin up Postgres temporarily in development and testing.

  • If your Go tests use Docker's postgres:latest image, note it now points at Postgres 19, so a new container using that image with a not yet upgraded v18 data volume will fail to start.

  • And while I'm on a run of Postgres updates, if you use Postgres at all, be sure to check out our sister newsletter Postgres Weekly!

issues.title: One Go GUI app, built five ways
issues.html:
#​625 — November 20, 2026


Read the Web Version



Go Weekly





Probabilistic Data Structures in Go — A diagram-driven tour of five probabilistic data structures (Bloom filters, count-min sketch, HyperLogLog, t-digest, top-k) that can use significantly less memory if approximate answers are sufficient (e.g. counting a million distinct strings in just 16KB of memory).

Anton Zhiyanov



💡 Anton has built unsure, a package that lets you use these structures easily.



ChatGPT Can Now React to Your MCP Server’s Events — MCP Events lets ChatGPT subscribe to events from your MCP server and act when they fire. Under the hood it’s webhooks: signed callbacks, retries, and subscriptions that expire. Here’s how it works, what the draft spec requires, and how to support it.

Svix sponsor



SIMD Support Looks Set to Graduate from Experimental Status — Last week we mentioned a proposal to graduate a large subset of Go's SIMD operations from experimental status. It's now marked 'likely accept'. The API design notes show what simd & simd/archsimd support on different platforms.

Austin Clements (Go Team)



IN BRIEF:

  • Go 1.28's development freeze starts on November 24, and the draft release notes are continuing to grow, most recently with go/analysis moving into the standard library.

  • Go 1.28's net/http Transport will manage HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 client connections in one pool, so connection limits will apply to both.

  • Michael Matloob proposes defaulting to toolchain-free cgo bindings when GOEXPERIMENT=cgobindings is enabled and CGO_ENABLED is unset.



How Resend Migrated Its Email API from Node to Go — Resend's team got tired of big JSON payloads blocking Node's event loop, so they rebuilt their API in Go and ran both versions while comparing responses until they matched. Huge CPU and memory wins also came from the move.

Resend



Go 1.28 Will Let You Write return {}, err — It's taken eleven years, but Go 1.28 is set to let you drop the type from a composite literal when it can be inferred by the compiler, so return {}, err will Just Work™. Redowan looks at where it does and doesn't apply, and addresses some worries over readability.

Redowan Delowar



Making Games with the Entity Component System Pattern — Miłosz has been building small games with Ebitengine and the Donburi ECS library, and this is what he's learned about structuring them, including when ECS gets in the way. Playable in-browser demos make it a fun read.

Miłosz Smółka (Three Dots Labs)



Build, Review, and Profile Go Code with Agents in GoLand — A hands-on look at Air, GoLand's new default AI workspace. Dominika builds a webhook receiver with Codex, Claude Code and Junie working in parallel worktrees, then lets an agent drive the profiler with a new skill.

Dominika Stankiewicz (JetBrains)



Turn Web Pages into Structured Data with SerpApi’s Extract API — Find pages with 100+ dedicated search engine APIs. Extract content as JSON or Markdown with a simple API.

SerpApi sponsor



📄 Compile-Checked Go Queries via Generic Methods – A look at how a new ORM uses Go 1.27's generic methods and pointers to struct fields as column names, so misspelled field names and mismatched value types can be caught by the compiler. Alberts Liepiņš

▶️ Go Without Wires: TinyGo on ESP32 – An Espressif DevCon talk on wireless communication with Go on ESP32 chips. "An aerial object may be involved…" Ron Evans

📄 Why Does gRPC Configure Clients with JSON? Kevin McDonald (Buf)

📄 How to Build a Coding Agent Harness in Go Jeff Bailey



🛠 Code & Tools





Comparing Go GUI Frameworks: One GUI App, Built Five Ways — Justin was struggling to pick a GUI toolkit from the Go ecosystem's increasing number of options, so he built the same app with Fyne, Cogent Core, Wails, templ+htmx and Qt, and compared the results against one another.

Justin Israel



🤖 Preconfigured Agents with Microsoft Agent Framework for Go — Microsoft Agent Framework for Go, currently in public preview, now includes an agent/harness package that wires up numerous things agents can benefit from (like to-do lists, skills, tool approvals, etc.).

Microsoft



  • Hugo 0.170 – The static site generator is now a single binary with no cgo, as the 'extended' edition (which needed to use libsass) is gone. (Sites that compile Sass now need Dart Sass installed.)

  • Huma 2.41 – The OpenAPI 3 and JSON Schema-backed REST/HTTP API framework can now expose operations as MCP tools.

  • Pion DTLS 4.0 – The pure Go DTLS library now defaults to DTLS 1.3. Jo Turk tells the story of how it got there.

  • fasthttp 1.79 – The fast HTTP package for Go now has a WebSocket server and client package of its own.

  • Telebot 4.0 – Telegram bot framework. Supports Bot API 10.4.



📰 Classifieds



Machine data in Go? Tiger Cloud brings automatic time partitioning and up to 95% compression to Postgres. Start with $1000 credit.

🦊 Give your AI agent 30+ PDF tools: Convert, extract, generate and sign over one MCP server. Works with Claude, Cursor and your own agents.



📢  Elsewhere in the ecosystem



  • 🐘 Postgres 19 came out yesterday, and if you use Postgres from Go, the new INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO SELECT is worth a look as it can give you 'get or create' functionality in a single query.

  • 🎓 Carnegie Mellon has started putting some of its computer science courses up on YouTube for anyone to watch, with lectures on things like software architecture, ML systems and building AI agents.

  • What did three weeks in GitHub's Secure Open Source Fund mean for modernc.org/sqlite? Jan Mercl, its maintainer, explains.

  • 📊 I don't hold much regard for TIOBE's programming language popularity index, but am still amused that Rust dropped out of the top 10 to be replaced by Go (which returns to the top 10 for the first time in over a year) 😎

issues.title: 'Go aims to be a steady hand on the tiller.'
issues.html:
#​624 — November 13, 2026


Read the Web Version



Go Weekly





Go Turns 17: An Update — A mini 'State of the Union' to celebrate Go's 17th birthday (first unveiled in a quite understated post in 2009). Austin recaps a year of Go improvements, but also looks ahead to 2027 with (a large subset of) SIMD graduating in 1.28, cutting Go's memory footprint "amid the global RAM crunch", and a reworked proposal process that will involve the Go community more.

Austin Clements (Go Team)



19 of 57 AI APIs Still Make You Poll for Job Results — That’s one finding in the State of Webhooks 2027. We scored 489 API companies, 66 of them AI API providers, against 17 criteria, from retries and signatures to how well agents can build on their events. Immediate download, no email required.

Svix sponsor



Inside PGO: What Go's Compiler Does With Your Profile — An illustrated dive behind the scenes of how Go's profile guided optimization feature operates. PGO is essentially a way to let the compiler optimize your app based on how it runs by inlining hot calls, aligning hot loops, and more.

Jesús Espino



💡 Lamplit Labs measured PGO on a log router and found 8.8-10% fewer instructions per line, all of it from inlining.



IN BRIEF:

  • 🔐 Go 1.27.4 and 1.26.11 have been released with twelve security fixes. Most of them prevent a malicious cgo dependency from running code at build time, and the stricter checks mean --sysroot and -target are no longer allowed in #cgo directives.

  • Go's new experimental generic collection types are ready to try in golang.org/x/exp/collection: sets, hashed maps, and the newly accepted sorted maps and sets. The Go team hopes to add them to the standard library in 1.29.

  • Austin Clements has proposed graduating a large subset of simd and simd/archsimd out of their experiment for Go 1.28, covering AMD64, ARM64 NEON, and WebAssembly.

  • Publishing the analyzer API as a go/analysis package in the standard library is now a 'likely accept', paving the way for go test to run your project's own analyzers.

  • ✈️ Tinyflight is TinyGo-based flight control firmware for the M5Stack StampFly 'mini quadcopter' (that you can also fly in a browser simulator here).



Catch Go Bugs That Fuzzing Misses with Gemini and a Constraint Solver — A delightfully technical post on Google's dev blog that highlights a shortcoming in Go's fuzzer where slice overruns can be missed (though a simple tweak can expose them), and experiments with a way to use Gemini and Z3 to find them directly.

Karl Weinmeister (Google)



CodeAF: 16 Coding Sessions in Half a Gigabyte, Written in Go — Each extra session adds 27 MB of RAM, 8x less than Claude Code. #1 of ten harnesses on DeepSWE, lowest cost per solve.

CodeAF by AgentField AI sponsor



📄 Go's JSON v1 vs v2 Under Load – MarshalWrite's many small writes cut one API's read throughput by 30%. Huseyin Babal

📄 Slashing a Go Service's Memory Use – Swapping map[string]bool sets for sorted []uint64 slices helped cut heap use by 78%. Ed Crewe

📄 A Hands-On Tour of What encoding/json/v2 Changes Christian Ekrem



🛠 Code & Tools





  • Lip Gloss 2.1 – Charm's terminal styling library. Tables can now size themselves to their content while still respecting a maximum width (as above).

  • Iris v14 – The veteran web framework's first major release since v12 now requires Go 1.27 so it can lean on generic methods.

  • checkescape – An introduction to gVisor's analyzer for enforcing zero allocations in annotated functions, à la the recently featured noalloc.

  • codemap – Generates a single interactive HTML visualization of a Go module's packages, dependencies, files, and functions.

  • ws 1.5 – The tiny, low-level WebSocket library adds SIMD-accelerated payload masking and stops trusting peer-declared payload lengths when allocating.

  • go-sqlite3 0.37 – cgo-free SQLite wrapper. database/sql transactions now default to BEGIN IMMEDIATE.

  • Fiber 3.7 – The Express-inspired web framework can now bind map fields from queries and forms.



📰 Classifieds



Billions of rows, one Postgres: TimescaleDB keeps your Go service’s analytics fast without a second database. $1000 credit on Tiger Cloud.

WarpBuild remote docker builders only rebuild what changed with optimized caching beyond just container layers. Get $50 in free credits with code START50.



📊  Go by the Numbers





Alongside Go's 17th birthday, JetBrains has published The State of Go in 2026, covering the results from developers who replied to its annual ecosystem survey and chose Go as one of their main languages. Among the stats for the Go-using respondents:

  • On the editor/IDE front, 14% are now using Zed, up nearly 3x from last year, with GoLand (49%) and VS Code (48%) neck and neck (though remember this is JetBrains' own survey :-)

  • 🤖 86% are using AI coding agents in the terminal on at least a weekly basis (versus 74% for all respondents, including non Go devs), with 55% saying most of their work code in the last month was generated by AI.

  • 46% now use net/http for web development, up from 32% a year ago and almost level with Gin (48%). chi (15%), Echo (13%), and Fiber (13%) follow.

  • 43% use TypeScript alongside Go in the same project, up from 24% in 2024. A Go backend with a TypeScript frontend is becoming de rigueur.

  • 25% say they've used Rust in the past year, but 70% have no plans to move away from Go. 🎉

There's a lot more than that in there, though, so… enjoy!
